stimulus.text:
Andrew Jackson, Farewell Address, March 4, 1837:

“At every hazard, and by every sacrifice, this Union must be preserved.”

“If the sordid feelings of mere selfishness shall usurp the place which ought to be filled by public spirit, the legislation of Congress will soon be converted into a scramble for personal and sectional advantages.”

Background: Jackson spoke as he left the presidency after two terms that included the nullification crisis of 1832–1833, when South Carolina tried to void the federal tariff.
stimulus.source_note: Quotations verbatim from Andrew Jackson, Farewell Address, March 4, 1837, public domain, as printed by the University of Texas Core Texts collection.

source: original; stimulus verbatim from Andrew Jackson, Farewell Address, March 4, 1837, public domain
stem: According to Jackson, what would turn Congress into 'a scramble for personal and sectional advantages'?

options.text: Too many states joining the Union at once
options.misconception: Jackson feared selfishness, not the number of states.

options.text: Lawmakers putting section first, ahead of the common good
The president vetoing too many bills in Congress
options.misconception: Jackson names selfishness in Congress, not vetoes by the president.

options.text: Foreign nations interfering in American trade
options.misconception: The passage is about selfishness at home, not interference from abroad.

rationales.A: Jackson warns about motives, not size. More states do not by themselves make a scramble.
rationales.B: Selfishness usurping public spirit means each section grabbing for itself. That is the scramble Jackson fears.
rationales.C: The veto is the president's tool, not Congress's. Jackson blames the spirit inside Congress itself.
rationales.D: No foreign nation appears in the passage. The scramble Jackson fears is made at home.
rationales.general:
1. Read the warning. Selfishness takes the place of public spirit, and then Congress scrambles for sectional gain.
2. Translate the words. Public spirit means serving the whole country; selfishness means serving your own section.
3. Name the cause. When lawmakers serve their section first, lawmaking becomes a scramble.
Remember: a warning about motives is a warning about what people will do next.
